native_mirror_before.title: Skryabin's equivalence for the type-A Whittaker pair
native_mirror_before.statement: The functor $Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}-\colon W(\lambda)\text{-mod}\to\mathcal C(\lambda)$ is an equivalence of categories, with inverse the Whittaker-vector functor $\mathrm{Wh}$; in particular $\mathrm{Wh}$ is exact and $\mathrm{Wh}(M)=0$ implies $M=0$ for $M\in\mathcal C(\lambda)$. For every finite dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module $X$, the exact functor $?\otimes X\colon\mathcal C(\lambda)\to\mathcal C(\lambda)$ transports to the exact functor $M\mapsto M\circledast X=\mathrm{Wh}((Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}M)\otimes X)$ on $W(\lambda)$-mod, and whenever $M$ is a $\mathfrak p$-module viewed as a $W(\lambda)$-module by restriction, the natural map $\mu_{M,X}\colon M\circledast X\to M\otimes X$, $(\eta(u)1_\chi\otimes m)\otimes x\mapsto um\otimes x$, is an isomorphism of $W(\lambda)$-modules. The associativity isomorphisms $(M\circledast X)\circledast Y\cong M\circledast(X\otimes Y)$ are compatible, and for the one dimensional $\mathfrak p$-module $\mathbb C_c$ the resulting isomorphism $\mu_d\colon\mathbb C_c\circledast V^{\circledast d}\to V_c^{\otimes d}$ is independent of the order of the composed associativity isomorphisms.
native_mirror_before.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. The preceding supplier computes invariants and higher cohomology of Qχ tensor_W X for arbitrary X, giving the unit isomorphism. For M in the locally nilpotent Whittaker category, apply invariants to the counit; its kernel/cokernel cannot be nonzero by the supplier's detection and cohomological lifting, so the counit is an isomorphism. Tensoring a finite-dimensional gl_N module preserves this category and is exact. To identify the transported tensor product with the ordinary tensor product on a p-module, solve the finite χ equations in PBW degree: the leading system is polynomial Taylor translation on C[M_unip], with invertible constant term. The finite matrices X,Y are inverse by degree recursion. Their source8.38 prefix-T formulas and finite inverse-column paths satisfy both tail and reflected-head χ systems, with the corrected reflected E/F recursion. This gives μ, its naturality and associativity, and matches the universal Casimir operators. The finite-W matrix proof §§3–4 gives the complete construction; no quoted Skryabin theorem is used as a missing prerequisite. In the prefix-T tensor matrices the mode is the actual displacement col(a)−col(b), as in source8.38; coefficients at or below the prefix shift vanish and coefficient0 is delta. No u^s reindexing occurs in X or its inverse Y.
